blocks.text: KING OF JUDAH · TWO KINGDOMS
Asa. Forty-one years in Jerusalem.
REIGNEDi
41 years c. 911–870 BC (dates vary)
CAPITAL
Jerusalem
HOUSE
House of David 3rd of 20 in Judah
VERDICT
✓ Did right “And Asa did that which was right in the eyes of the LORD, as did David his father.”
PROPHETS
Azariah son of Oded · Hanani the seer
JUDAH (THE SOUTH): 20 RULERS REHOBOAM → ZEDEKIAH
SUCCESSION
The two kingdoms
THE VERDICT
How Scripture judges the reign
“And Asa did that which was right in the eyes of the LORD, as did David his father.”
1 Kings 15:11 (KJV) →
“nevertheless Asa’s heart was perfect with the LORD all his days”
1 Kings 15:14 (KJV) →
BUT ALSO
But also: "the high places were not removed". 1 Kings 15:14 2 Chronicles 15:17
Chronicles adds that when he relied on the king of Syria against Baasha, Hanani the seer rebuked him; Asa put him in prison and "oppressed some of the people". 2 Chronicles 16:7–10
Chronicles adds that in his disease "he sought not to the LORD, but to the physicians". 2 Chronicles 16:12
CHRONICLES GIVES IT AS
“And Asa did that which was good and right in the eyes of the LORD his God”
2 Chronicles 14:2 (KJV) →
JUDAH (THE SOUTH): 20 RULERS
✓ Did right ✕ Did evil ◐ Mixed ● No verdict formula
THE KINGDOM
Jerusalem and the places of the reign
Judah (the south) · tribe of Judah. Only places Scripture names are shown, each where the Atlas puts it.
EVENTS
Wars, works and turning points
Each mark sits at the year of the reign the Bible gives for it.
UNDATED IN SCRIPTURE
THE NATION
What the nation did
Idols and the sodomites removed; the queen mother's idol burnt. 1 Kings 15:12–13
A covenant to seek the LORD, with death for whoever would not (Chronicles). 2 Chronicles 15:12–13
Yet the high places were not removed. 1 Kings 15:14
PROPHETS
Prophets of the reign
Az Azariah son of Oded “The LORD is with you, while ye be with him; and if ye seek him, he will be found of you; but if ye forsake him, he will forsake you.”
Ha Hanani the seer “Herein thou hast done foolishly: therefore from henceforth thou shalt have wars.”
ON THE WORLD STAGE
The powers of the day
ARAM (DAMASCUS)
Ben-hadad son of Tabrimon
CUSH (ETHIOPIA)
Zerah the Ethiopian
TWO ACCOUNTS
Where Kings and Chronicles differ
Each ribbon joins the two accounts of one matter, passage to passage.

1 KINGS
2 CHRONICLES
War and peace
1 KINGS
2 CHRONICLES
The high places

DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
41 years (1 Kgs 15:10). Scripture gives lengths and cross-dates, never BC years.
THIELE, REVISED BY MCFALL (1991)
Printed form: 911/910–870/869 (PDF p. 11).
YOUNG (2005), REVISING THIELE
ALBRIGHT (1945)
Printed form: c. 913–873 (p. 20).
TRADITIONAL DATES (USSHER, 1658)
Printed form: 955–914 (p. 42 (scan leaf n26)). The 1658 margin misprints the year as 965 [sic]; its own year-of-the-world column gives 955.
Raised him, so called mother
John Gill (1748–63)
She is called his mother "not because she brought him forth, but because she brought him up". 1 Kings 15:10 [107]
Grandmother who kept the queen mother's office
C. F. Keil (1872)
Abijam's mother Maachah stayed queen mother into Asa's reign, perhaps because Asa's own mother died early, until he deposed her. 1 Kings 15:10 1 Kings 15:13 [22]
Hard to solve; perhaps the grandmother kept her place
Pulpit Commentary (1881), after K. Bähr's doubt

Bähr doubted that the Hebrew word for mother can mean grandmother here. The note grants that the difficulty "by no means admits of a ready solution", but suggests the best explanation is that the grandmother kept her position, perhaps because Asa's own mother was dead. 1 Kings 15:10 [78]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 5
1 Kings 15 1 Kings 16 2 Chronicles 14 2 Chronicles 15 2 Chronicles 16
PASSAGES · 10
1 Kings 15:8–24 1 Kings 15:25 1 Kings 15:33 1 Kings 16:8 1 Kings 16:15 1 Kings 16:23 1 Kings 16:29 2 Chronicles 14:1–15 2 Chronicles 15:1–19 2 Chronicles 16:1–14
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not give Asa's age when he began to reign.
Scripture does not name Asa's disease beyond its being "in his feet".
Scripture does not say who Zerah the Ethiopian served or where he came from beyond "Ethiopians and Lubims".
